# Decides WHICH RACE a child of mixed parentage is. It does not decide what the child looks like:
# that is gfx/portraits/portrait_modifiers/99_gen_race_morphs.txt (a generated file — see
# Emit/RaceMorphWriter.cs), which forces the race-defining genes by trait at render time while
# everything else — nose, eyes, mouth, cheeks, hair, colouring — blends from the parents normally.
#
# History of this file, because the failure mode is worth remembering: an earlier version ran
# `copy_inheritable_appearance_from` on EVERY birth in the game, unguarded. On a human map that made
# every child a genetic near-clone of one randomly chosen parent, flattening family variation
# world-wide; inside a race it made siblings identical; and it copied whole genomes across sexes,
# which vanilla itself only ever does behind a `sex_same_as` check. Dropping the genome copy — and
# letting the portrait modifier carry the race instead — fixes all three at once, and covers the
# engine-generated characters the birth hook can never see.

gen_resolve_child_phenotype_effect = {
	# Nothing to decide unless a race is actually in play. On a human-only map no character ever
	# carries a phenotype trait, so this is one trigger per birth and no further cost — which is
	# also what keeps the human marker flag out of non-fantasy worlds entirely.
	if = {
		limit = {
			OR = {
				mother ?= { gen_has_phenotype_trigger = yes }
				real_father ?= { gen_has_phenotype_trigger = yes }
			}
		}

		# One parent is chosen and the child takes their race whole. When both parents are the same
		# race the coin flip is a no-op, so it needs no special case; when one is human the child
		# has an even chance of coming out human, which is what makes a mixed line thin out over
		# generations instead of every descendant staying fantastical.
		if = {
			limit = {
				exists = mother
				exists = real_father
			}
			random_list = {
				50 = { gen_take_parent_race_effect = { PARENT = mother } }
				50 = { gen_take_parent_race_effect = { PARENT = real_father } }
			}
		}
		else_if = {
			limit = { exists = mother }
			gen_take_parent_race_effect = { PARENT = mother }
		}
		else_if = {
			limit = { exists = real_father }
			gen_take_parent_race_effect = { PARENT = real_father }
		}
	}
}

# Copies one parent's race onto the newborn.
#
# Written as an else_if chain rather than six independent ifs so a parent who somehow carries two
# phenotypes — the `opposites` lists are meant to prevent it, but the ruler designer and the console
# can still produce one — hands over exactly one instead of stacking them onto the child.
gen_take_parent_race_effect = {
	$PARENT$ = { save_scope_as = gen_race_donor }

	if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_gracile } }
		add_trait = phenotype_gracile
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_stocky } }
		add_trait = phenotype_stocky
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_rough_hewn } }
		add_trait = phenotype_rough_hewn
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_towering } }
		add_trait = phenotype_towering
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_diminutive } }
		add_trait = phenotype_diminutive
	}
	else_if = {
		limit = { scope:gen_race_donor = { has_trait = phenotype_dusk_adapted } }
		add_trait = phenotype_dusk_adapted
	}
	else = {
		# The chosen donor is human. Say so explicitly: an unmarked child is indistinguishable from
		# one the birth hook never reached, and the yearly pulse would hand it the local culture's
		# race — overruling the parents, which is the one thing that must always win at birth.
		# A flag rather than a trait so it shows nowhere — see 00_phenotype_triggers.txt.
		add_character_flag = gen_phenotype_human
	}
}
